title: Starting values for agent placement/routing when project, fab and vendor data are silent
how_to_use: Precedence: project constraints > fab capability > device-specific vendor guide > these starting values.
A starting value is NOT a pass/fail standard. 'target' is what the agent aims for; beyond 'review' the agent must either fix the layout or write a justification in the review report.
Every starting value the agent actually uses must be listed in layout_intent.json under 'assumptions' with the id below, so the owner can see what was assumed.
basis: VENDOR = stated in a cited vendor document; CALC = computed from a stated formula; PRACTICE = common engineering practice, not verified against a source in this repository.

fab_profile_fallback.note: Deliberately looser than typical prototype-fab minimums so the board stays manufacturable at most fabs. Replace with the real fab's numbers as soon as they are known (rule A02).

track_width_by_current.formula: IPC-2221 external conductor: I = 0.048 * dT^0.44 * A^0.725 (A in mil^2), 1 oz copper, dT = 10 C; value then rounded up to a convenient width. Same formula as the KiCad PCB Calculator track-width tab.
track_width_by_current.note: Thermal sizing only. Always also check voltage drop (D-VDROP). For 2 oz copper the calculated width halves. Above 5 A use a filled zone/polygon and a project-specific calculation (rule R04).
track_width_by_current.gnd_return_rule: The return (GND) path of a load must be at least as wide as its supply path; on a 2-layer board that means a filled GND zone, not a thin GND track.

voltage_drop.formula: R = rho * L / (w * t), rho = 1.72e-8 ohm*m at 20 C, t = 35 um per oz; 1 oz sheet resistance ~0.49 mOhm/square. Vdrop = I * R summed over supply and return.

vias_at_layer_change.count_rule: n = max(2, ceil(I_continuous / current_per_via)) for every place a power or GND-return path changes layer.
placement_rule: Spread the vias across the WIDTH of the copper, in at most 2-3 staggered rows; do not line them up single-file along the current direction.
Change layer on a straight section, not in a corner; in a corner only the inside-corner vias carry current.
Keep copper between pad and via group at least as wide as the track itself (no neck-down).
Solid connection to zones for these vias; no thermal-relief spokes.
Leave copper between antipads on inner planes so the via group does not cut a slot in GND.
Put vias next to the component pin where current enters/leaves.
vias_at_layer_change.note: TS14 lists 0.84 A for a 12 mil via and 1.1 A for a 16 mil via at 10 C rise on 1 oz. TS15 shows via temperature follows the attached copper, so the count is driven by voltage drop, inductance and redundancy, not by fear of fusing.

decoupling.note: Distance is a proxy for loop inductance (rule P04 / PT03). Measured pad-to-pad from the IC supply pad to the capacitor pad on the same net, plus capacitor GND pad to the IC GND pad or to its GND via.

switching_converter.note: The converter's own datasheet layout figure overrides everything here (PT02).

crystal.note: Vendor guide first (PT04). ESP32-S3 (RD03) wants at least 2.0 mm between crystal and clock pin; do not carry that number to other MCUs.

esd_protection.order: connector pin -> TVS pad -> rest of circuit (the track must pass the TVS pad, not branch to it with a stub)

differential_pair.note: Impedance needs the real stackup (R07, TS03). On a generic 1.6 mm 2-layer board 90 ohm differential is usually not achievable with practical widths: route short, coupled, over solid GND and report the limitation instead of certifying impedance.

two_layer_reference_plane.note: On 2 layers one side (normally B.Cu) is the GND reference. A track on that side is a slot in the plane.

return_via.applies_to: clock, differential pair and fast-edge nets that change reference plane on 4+ layer boards
